title: Generativity through supporting conditions
user_steering: being generative needs conditions, if there is no sun there is no us on the planet, please explore into this direction.
interpretation: Supporting conditions are part of the relational foundation. Investigate usable energy, retention, conversion, renewal and timing without requiring local self-sufficiency or substituting a normative thesis.

claim_status.constant_power_threshold: Proved global active-material decay at and below Pc=loss*b/(k*M); existence, uniqueness and local asymptotic stability of positive equilibrium above Pc.
claim_status.positive_global_attraction: Not proved for the extended energy model.
claim_status.same_mean_timing_counterexample: Proved in the same supplied-power model: constant1.2 has stable positive equilibrium; 2.4 for30 then0 for30 globally extinguishes active material from every finite initial energy reserve.
claim_status.contraction_certificate: Analytic positive matrix bound with an explicit eventual reserve envelope2.41; strict upper bound verified independently and via rational/Taylor inequalities.
claim_status.energy_balance: Exact reduced work-equivalent balance, not a complete molecular thermodynamic realization.
claim_status.entropy_scope: Net entropy export conclusion restricted to bounded/sublinear entropy storage and existing long-run averages.
claim_status.current_state: Supply phase can be included as a physical state coordinate; mean input alone discards causal information.
claim_status.universal_root: Working conceptual formulation; not a proof of all generativity, open-ended novelty, the physical reaction repertoire, or universal direction toward kindness.

checks.simulation_method: Fourth-order Runge-Kutta, steps .01 and .005; every supply switch aligned to step boundary.

checks.claims: Proofs establish threshold and collapse; trajectories illustrate one initial state and do not establish positive global attraction.

visual_review.method: Viewed rendered PNG twice; moved upper legend to eliminate interference with supply curve.
visual_review.outcome: Axes, captions, threshold, logarithmic activity scale and legends readable; no clipping observed.

reviews.type: Independent reasoning reviews by three collaborating AI agents, not external scientific peer review.
reviews.outcome: Mathematical results and physical scope passed. One entropy-scope refinement applied.
reviews.applied_refinement: Changed unqualified sustained-activity entropy export claim to bounded steady dissipative operation.

sources.scope: Full read; base material-renewal model, energy reserve limitation, and sufficient-present discussion.

sources.author: Axel Kleidon
sources.title: How does the Earth system generate and maintain thermodynamic disequilibrium and what does it imply for the future of the planet?
sources.version_read: 2011 author manuscript, arXiv1103.2014v2; reviewer identifies later2012 publication.
sources.scope: Parent read returned text through section3.2, including boundaries, balances, photon conversion and free-energy transfer. Reviewer inspected sections2–4.5. Main report uses only disequilibrium, conversion and entropy-balance claims.
sources.excluded: No adoption of maximum entropy production as a universal law, no present-day numerical planetary estimates imported, no claim that the paper proves our model.

limitations: All rates and timings in the comparison are dimensionless; no planetary or organism fit.
Continuous deterministic concentrations do not imply indefinite finite-particle survival.
Asymptotic depletion does not establish finite-time disappearance.
Capture, storage construction and feedback on the source are not endogenous in this extension.
Numerical trajectories are illustrations; no new empirical experiment was performed.
